title: Subeg Singh fears a saint's curse

blocks.text: The Nawab’s plea reaches Subeg Singh, who listens but does not rush to intercede. He warns that the Khalsa Panth alone could arbitrate the ruler’s fate, because no courtier can casually overturn a saint’s judgment.

Subeg Singh also fears that merely carrying the Nawab's case might expose his own household to ruin if Bhai Taru Singh refuses. The Nawab therefore has to abase himself further, touching feet and pleading for someone willing to take the risk.
This page slows the story into moral deliberation rather than instant rescue. Even sympathy for suffering cannot erase what the Nawab has done or the spiritual hierarchy now standing over him.
